Definition: Percentage of the national population covered by at least one 4G/LTE mobile network signal, whether or not they subscribe to the service. 4G is the practical minimum for meaningful broadband connectivity enabling digital services.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source was an SSA-wide GSMA blog, not Tanzania-specific. TCRA regulator data (via The Citizen) shows 4G population coverage rising from 79% (Dec 2023) to 83% (Jun 2024), and a Tanzania-specific ITU/TCRA workshop slide gives 94.2% (more recent). This is well above the 50-74% band, so revised to 90%+ (code 5); note ITU's 2024 IDI separately cites a lower normalised figure (58%), so a human check against the latest TCRA quarterly release is advisable.

Definition: Affordability of mobile broadband data, measured as the cost of a basic mobile data plan (1-2GB) as a percentage of GNI per capita. The UN Broadband Commission target is below 2% of monthly GNI per capita. Affordability is the single largest barrier to internet adoption in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source discussed continent-wide affordability, not Tanzania specifically. A Tanzania-specific ITU LDC report figure puts the data-only mobile-broadband basket at roughly 2% of GNI per capita, which sits right at the boundary between 'Moderate' (2-5%) and 'Affordable' (1-2%). Code 3 kept as the best estimate but flagged for human review given the boundary value and difficulty parsing the exact ITU table.

revision_notes: World Bank data show internet use rising from 29.1% (2023) to 31.16% (2024); DataReportal's Digital 2024 report gives 31.9% (Jan 2024). The original comment mis-stated 29.1% as falling in the 30-49% band (it does not), but the freshest 2024 figures (~31%) do support code 3, so it is confirmed with corrected reasoning and updated sourcing.

Definition: The country's total international internet bandwidth capacity per internet user, indicating the quality and capacity of the country's connection to the global internet. Determined by submarine cable landings (for coastal states), cross-border terrestrial fibre (for landlocked states), and satellite links.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original ITU source is a generic global bandwidth-usage report page, not Tanzania-specific — confirmed unrelated to the country as flagged. The only Tanzania-specific data located (2012-2016, averaging 3.6 kbit/s per user) is too dated to support a current score, and no current ITU DataHub/TeleGeography figure could be retrieved within the available search budget. Set to Unknown (0); recommend human review using ITU DataHub's current international-bandwidth-per-user series for Tanzania.

Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
Comments: TIX Dar es Salaam active moderate. [Cloudscene](https://cloudscene.com/market/data-centers-in-tanzania/dar-es-salaam)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: PeeringDB and Internet Society's IXP tracker (2026) show TIX Dar es Salaam with 32+ peering ASNs, including major global content networks (Meta, Akamai), 708G total capacity, and continuous operation since 2003. This constitutes broad participation at a mature single IXP, supporting an upgrade from 'moderate participation' (4) to 'mature ecosystem with broad participation' (5).

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The original comment conflates 'unique subscriber' penetration with total mobile connections/SIM penetration (TCRA reports 99-111%+ of population, which counts multiple SIMs per person). Corroborating evidence (very high connection penetration, DataReportal 2024/2025 reports) is consistent with genuinely high unique-subscriber penetration, so code 5 (70%+) is retained, but the precise GSMA Intelligence unique-subscriber figure is paywalled and was not independently confirmed — recommend a human check against GSMA Intelligence direct data.

redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: TCRA's own quarterly device-penetration data (Tanzania-specific, more authoritative than the generic GSMA Sub-Saharan Africa regional estimate used originally) shows smartphone penetration of 31.55% (Jun 2024), 33.85% (Sep 2024) and 35.99% (Dec 2024) — all within the 20-39% band, below the 40-59% originally recorded. Revised down to code 2; a later, unconfirmed figure near 42% was also seen and should be checked against the latest TCRA release.

Africa's startup scene is well-documented by trackers like Partech, Disrupt Africa, and Briter Bridges.

This corroborates a 'developing' ecosystem (code 3) with more authoritative sources, though funding remains highly concentrated in very few deals.
